---

## 🥤 Cocaine in Coca-Cola: The Full Story

### The Origins
Coca-Cola was invented in 1885 by John Pemberton, a pharmacist from Atlanta, Georgia, who made the original formula in his backyard. Pemberton's recipe contained cocaine in the form of an extract of the coca leaf, which inspired the "Coca" part of the beverage's name.

Coke was originally sold as a patent medicine, and cocaine was a common medicinal ingredient used widely by physicians at the time. Cocaine tonics, powders and pills were popularly believed to cure a variety of ailments, from headache and fatigue to constipation, nausea, asthma and impotence.

### How Much Cocaine Was in It?
Coca-Cola once contained an estimated **nine milligrams of cocaine per glass**. For comparison, a typical dose or "line" of cocaine is 50–75 mg.

### Why Was It Removed?
Within just a decade of Coca-Cola's creation, public attitudes regarding cocaine changed dramatically. This had everything to do with the drug's adoption by the southern Black working class. Asa Candler (who had taken over the company) fought back against the damage that cocaine's declining reputation did to his brand, arguing that the small quantity of coca extract in Coke was merely energizing. He also leaned into an emphasis on the soda as a "refreshing" and "great tasting" drink, downplaying its supposed medicinal qualities.

Cocaine was not made illegal in the United States until 1914. In 1903, the fresh coca leaves were removed from the formula.

### Was It Fully Removed Right Away?
Not entirely. Some amount of coca extract was retained as an ingredient in order to protect the trade name "Coca-Cola." Candler believed that his product's name had to be descriptive, and that he must have at least some by-product of the coca leaf in the syrup to protect his right to the name Coca-Cola.

By 1902, the amount was as little as 1/400 of a grain of cocaine per ounce of syrup. Coke wouldn't become completely cocaine-free until 1929, when scientists perfected the process of removing all psychoactive elements from coca-leaf extract.

### Does Coca-Cola Still Use Coca Leaves Today?
Yes — but without the cocaine. Coca-Cola uses a coca leaf extract made by the Stepan Company at its Maywood, New Jersey plant. This facility is the only place in the U.S. authorized by the Drug Enforcement Administration to import coca leaves, mostly from Peru and Bolivia. The Stepan Company removes the cocaine through a very complex process, creating a cocaine-free extract that goes to Coca-Cola for their drinks. The leftover cocaine is sold to Mallinckrodt, the only pharmaceutical company in the United States licensed to purify cocaine for medical uses.

---

**In short:** Yes, early Coca-Cola did contain real cocaine, but in relatively small amounts. It was gradually phased out in the early 1900s and completely eliminated by 1929. Today's Coke still uses coca leaf extract, but with all cocaine chemically removed.
